prompt:
Write 7 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a parking lot collision claim, in time order. Injury: knee injury. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1206; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- It is not yet clear whether the injury came from this crash.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- It is not fully clear where in the vehicle the claimant was sitting.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: Claim received for a low-speed collision in a parking lot involving the insured vehicle and a second vehicle. The claimant is represented by counsel, so all further contact goes through the attorney's office.

Entry 2: Reviewed the policy and confirmed the driver is named on it and coverage was in force at the time of the loss. Nothing in the file suggests the damage predates the policy start.

Entry 3: Obtained statements from the other driver and two witnesses, and all of them describe the collision the same way. Photos taken at the scene are consistent with that description.

Entry 4: Vehicle damage was inspected and matches the reported impact pattern. No earlier damage to the vehicle has come up in prior claims or in the inspection.

Entry 5: The claimant reports a knee injury from the collision. Records show no previous injury to the same area, though it is not yet clear where the claimant was seated in the vehicle, and the medical link to this crash is still under review.

Entry 6: Medical records show treatment that followed a typical course and eased off as the claimant improved. The claimant has given the same account of events in every conversation so far.

Entry 7: Current status: liability is clear on the facts gathered, while the injury causation question remains open pending the treating provider's written opinion. Next step is to send the medical file to the reviewer and continue correspondence through counsel.
